# WEB-TOOLS ENGINEER — Findings & Recommendation

Deliverable file (copy-pasteable, zero-dep, matches your `tool.js`/`registry.js`/`notebook.js` conventions): **`C:\Users\andro\OneDrive\Desktop\gen\sidecar\tools\builtin\web.js`** — exports `makeWebTools(deps)` → `{ searchTool, fetchTool, webSearch(query), webFetch(url), register(registry) }`. Validated offline (parser, SSRF guard, fallback chain all pass) and against live endpoints (below).

## Live evidence gathered (June 2026, real requests from this Windows box)

| Endpoint | Result | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `POST html.duckduckgo.com/html/` | **200, real results** on a cold IP | Markup: `<a class="result__a" href="//duckduckgo.com/l/?uddg=<ENCODED-URL>">`, snippet in `<a class="result__snippet">`. Must URL-decode the `uddg=` param to get the real link. |
| Same, after ~3-5 rapid calls | **202, "anomaly"/"challenge" shell, 0 results** | The IP stays blocked for **minutes** (still 202 after 45s+ cooldown). This is the #1 reliability risk. |
| `lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/` | Same 202 anomaly once IP is flagged | Different markup (`result-link`) but **shares the same IP-level block**, so it's a weak fallback, not an independent one. |
| `r.jina.ai/<url>` (Jina Reader) | **200, clean text, NO key** | Keyless = **20 RPM**, free key = 500 RPM. `X-Return-Format: text` gives clean plain text. **Surfaces upstream errors inside a 200 body**: `Warning: Target URL returned error 404` — must scan body, not just status. |
| `s.jina.ai` (Jina Search) | **401 AuthenticationRequiredError** | **Changed in 2026 — now requires an API key.** Not viable for keyless MVP. Don't use it. |
| OpenRouter web search | Works via `tools:[{type:"openrouter:web_search",parameters:{engine:"auto",max_results:N}}]` | **`:online` suffix is now deprecated.** ~**$0.005/request** (Exa/Parallel, up to 10 results, +$0.001/extra). Results come back as `message.annotations[].url_citation`. Hides the search as one model turn (bad for your "watch the agent search" goal) but very robust. |

## PRIMARY recommendation

**`web_search` → DuckDuckGo HTML endpoint**, parsed to `[{title,url,snippet}]`, with mandatory guards:
- Detect the 202/"anomaly" shell and treat as a soft failure (don't return the empty shell as "no results").
- **Self-throttle** (the code is structured for it; add a per-run min-interval, ~1 req/sec, and a per-run search cap — you already have per-run tool-call caps in the loop).
- Fallback chain: **DDG-html → DDG-lite → OpenRouter `openrouter:web_search`** (only if the user's OpenRouter key is wired in via `deps.openrouter`).

**`web_fetch` → Jina Reader (`r.jina.ai/<url>`)**, keyless, clean markdown/text, with fallback to **direct fetch + HTML-strip** (`htmlToText`, no rate limit, great for static pages). Jina is primary because it handles JS-heavy/messy pages far better than regex-stripping; direct-fetch is the always-available safety net.

## Fallback chains (implemented)

- **web_search:** `duckduckgo-html` → `duckduckgo-lite` → `openrouter:web_search`. Each path that throws/returns 0 is recorded; only if all fail does it throw with a combined reason.
- **web_fetch:** `jina` → `direct fetch + strip`. Jina 401/402/429 or in-body upstream-error warning triggers the direct fallback; empty Jina output also falls through.

## Security (built in)

- SSRF guard on `web_fetch`: rejects non-http(s) and `localhost`/`127.*`/`10.*`/`192.168.*`/`172.16-31.*`/`169.254.*` (cloud metadata)/`::1`/`.local`/`.internal`. Verified it blocks all 5 attack URLs and allows public ones.
- All network calls are `AbortController`-time-bounded (search 12s, fetch 15s); tool `timeoutMs` set above the internal budget so the registry's outer timeout is a backstop, not the primary.
- Output truncated (web_fetch ~6k chars, snippets ~320). No keys/secrets are ever logged.
- Tools emit `tool.web` events (`search`, `search.results`, `fetch`, `fetch.done`) so the game can show the agent searching/reading in real time — exactly your "show the agent working" goal. These use `ctx.emit`, matching the notebook tool's pattern. **Note:** you'll need a `tool.web` event added to your `shared/events.js` schema, or repurpose an existing event name, or the validated emitter may reject it.

## ToS / reliability risks (flag)

- **DDG HTML scraping is against DuckDuckGo's ToS and is rate-limit-fragile** — fine for a local single-user BYOK MVP, but it *will* intermittently 202-block under bursty use. The code degrades gracefully; it does not pretend the block didn't happen.
- **Jina Reader keyless = 20 RPM** and is a third-party proxy (your fetched URLs transit Jina's servers — a privacy consideration worth a one-line note in your UI). Adding a free Jina key (`deps.jinaKey`, already supported in the code) raises it to 500 RPM.
- **Jina Search is dead for keyless** as of 2026 — do not build on it.

## What a production version swaps to

Wire a real search API key behind the same `webSearch()` interface (the fallback chain is already the right shape): **Brave Search API** (2k free queries/mo, cleanest ToS), **Tavily** (LLM-agent-optimized, returns snippets ready for context), or **Serper** (cheap Google SERP). Make DDG the *fallback* and the keyed API the *primary* once a key exists. For `web_fetch`, a self-hosted readability extractor (Mozilla Readability / Trafilatura) removes the Jina dependency and the privacy hop. The module is structured so adding `deps.search = {provider, apiKey}` as the first link in the chain is a ~15-line change.

One integration note for whoever wires this up: register with `makeWebTools({ openrouter: { apiKey: userKey, model } }).register(registry)` and add a `web` capability to `sidecar/capability/registry.js` so the cap-gate grants `web_search`/`web_fetch` (they're tagged `capability:'web'`).
